semantic_correction.stem: A client newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes understands the medication prescription but says, ‘I don’t know how to fit glucose monitoring, meals, activity, and problem-solving into daily life.’ Which referral would most directly address this need?

options.A: Refer the client to a diabetes self-management education and support service for individualized self-care skills, goal setting, and problem-solving support.
options.B: Refer the client for medical nutrition therapy focused on meal planning, while leaving glucose monitoring, activity planning, and broader self-management for routine visits.
options.C: Refer the client to a medication-management service focused on prescription review, while deferring daily self-care skills and behavior-change planning to later follow-up.
options.D: Delay an education referral until the client has difficulty meeting treatment goals, then arrange structured self-management teaching as a response to that problem.

semantic_correction.rationale: The 2026 American Diabetes Association Standards of Care advise all people with diabetes to participate in diabetes self-management education and support (DSMES) and specifically identify diagnosis as a critical time to provide DSMES. DSMES supports informed decision-making, self-care behaviors, problem-solving, active collaboration with the health care team, goal setting, and behavior-change strategies. The client is asking how to integrate multiple self-management tasks into daily life, so A most directly addresses the stated need. B can be valuable for nutrition but is narrower than the client's combined monitoring, activity, and problem-solving needs. C focuses on medication review even though the client already understands the prescription and does not provide the broader self-management support requested. D incorrectly postpones DSMES despite diagnosis itself being a recommended time for participation.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Refer clients with diabetes to DSMES for individualized education and support in self-care skills, problem-solving, goal setting, and sustainable health behaviors beginning at diagnosis and again at other critical times of need.
semantic_correction.source_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee for Diabetes
semantic_correction.source_document_title: 5. Facilitating Positive Health Behaviors and Well-being to Improve Health Outcomes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
semantic_correction.source_version_date: Diabetes Care 2026;49(Supplement 1):S89–S124; published December 8, 2025; live article rechecked August 20, 2026

semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: DSMES is recommended for people with diabetes beginning at diagnosis and directly supports the combined self-management, problem-solving, goal-setting, and behavior-change needs described in the stem.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup retained the DSMES-referral construct, removed the original all/only distractor cues, rebuilt the alternatives as plausible competing referral pathways, and removed the uniquely-long correct answer while preserving diagnosis as an ADA-supported critical time for DSMES.

scope_exclusions.credential: The item does not require a specific professional credential or claim that one credential alone defines every DSMES program.
scope_exclusions.prescribing_scope: No universal prescribing-authority or state scope-of-practice claim is tested.
scope_exclusions.nutrition: Medical nutrition therapy is valuable diabetes care but is presented as narrower than the combined self-management needs explicitly stated in this stem.
scope_exclusions.coverage: No insurance, reimbursement, referral-authorization, or payer rule is tested.
scope_exclusions.frequency: The item tests referral at diagnosis; it does not require memorization of every later DSMES reassessment interval.
scope_exclusions.treatment_plan: The client already understands the medication prescription, so the construct is self-management education/support rather than medication selection or titration.

near_duplicate_check.note: Targeted GitHub search for ‘DSMES diagnosis problem-solving goal setting diabetes self-management referral’ returned no indexed repository match. No broad bank scan was performed.

option_audit.A: Correct. DSMES is specifically designed to integrate self-care knowledge, skills, problem-solving, goals, and sustained behavior support beginning at diagnosis.
option_audit.B: Plausible because nutrition therapy is important in type 2 diabetes, but it does not by itself most directly cover the full monitoring, activity, and problem-solving need stated in the stem.
option_audit.C: Plausible because medication management is part of diabetes care, but it does not match the client's expressed gap after medication understanding is already established.
option_audit.D: Plausible because DSMES is also appropriate when treatment goals are not met, but ADA identifies diagnosis itself as a critical time rather than requiring delay.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. B and C are legitimate partial referrals but are intentionally narrower than the client's explicit multi-domain self-management need. D delays an intervention recommended at diagnosis. A is the only option that directly addresses the whole need described.

cueing_check.note: The key is not longest; all four options are referral decisions with comparable detail and no all/only/always/never/every cue.

blueprint_audit.entry_level_relevance: NCSBN explicitly includes assessing referral needs, collaborating with multidisciplinary team members, and using referral/community resources under Management of Care, making this an entry-level RN coordination-of-care construct.
